_README: Every human judgement about this ROM lives in this file; the
generated listings are disposable, so renaming is free.
What to do next, roughly in order:
Read the coverage it reports. Low coverage is normal at
first and is the number you are trying to move.
2. Every unresolved indirect jump it reports is a hole. Add the
target to `entries`, or the pointer pair to `ram_vectors` if
the handler is installed into RAM.
Finds the sound code and the tables feeding it.
4. Name things in `labels` as soon as you know what they are.
See docs/method.md for the working order and docs/pitfalls.md for
the traps that each cost real time.

comments.rom:C2AB: ENTRY_Irq: the IRQ vector points at the RTI that closes DLI stage 1 (VEC_C298, $C298-$C2AB), so a stray IRQ or BRK just returns. Corrected 2026-11-08: earlier notes call this a lone one-byte RTI, an isolated code island inside the character sheet; it is the last byte of the handler.
comments.rom:D8D5: Per-slot init (X=0..2): zeroes Score0/1/2Team/3Extra (rom:sub_D8D5 -- CONFIRMED score storage: sub_DDA9/sub_DE1C below do SED/ADC BCD arithmetic directly into these four fields). Then seeds ram_2119/ram_211A/ram_211B from dat_D97D,X where X=ram_1FCB.
comments.rom:DDA9: CONFIRMED (SED at rom:DDAE, BCD arithmetic): adds the caller's A/Y-held BCD point value into Score0/1/2Team/3Extra for slot X, doubling the add when ram_2122==3 (a bonus-multiplier state). Falls through to sub_DE1C's extra-life check on every score change -- not a separate poll. RETRACTION (cross-checked against a private, unofficial preserved-source archive of GCC's original 1984 assembly for this game -- not redistributed or quoted verbatim, used only to sanity-check our own independent reads; see docs/FINDINGS.md for how this is being handled): the earlier note called Score0/1/2Team/3Extra 'four BCD digit places across three player slots.' That was wrong in kind, not just detail -- each of the four is its own 3-byte BCD number (player-0 score, player-1 score, a team score for 2-player co-op, and a spare block used by the high-score cart), and the X=0..2 index selects a byte *within* one number, not a player. Independently re-checked against our own listing, not just taken on the reference's word.
comments.rom:DE1C: Extra-life threshold check, run after every score add (see rom:DDA9). Subtracts NextLifeThreshold{Lo,Hi},X from the score; if the score has reached it, advances the threshold by BCD $0120 and -- if LivesRemaining,X is still under 6 and the ram_00DE,X bit-6 flag isn't set -- increments LivesRemaining,X (the actual life award). LIVE-OBSERVED (tools/probe-ram-snapshots.lua, run-01.inp): ram_210E (slot 0, the only active slot in this 1-player recording) moves through 0/1/2 across the session rather than sitting still, consistent with real awards happening, matching the user's report of getting extra lives. RETRACTION: previously named ExtraLifeAwardCount on the theory it counted bonuses given, not lives held; cross-checked against a private reference archive (see rom:DDA9's note on how that's being used) and independently confirmed against ram_00DE's role (ObjectStatus+14, the shooter's status byte -- bit 6 there gates something else entirely, not a 'no more bonuses' flag as guessed before) -- renamed to LivesRemaining, the field this session's own live data was already consistent with, just mislabeled.
comments.rom:D840: The main per-frame loop (jumped back into from rom:D86E after an NMI-synced wait on ram_2108 bit7). Runs, in order: sub_E25E (coin/start-switch and attract-mode front end), sub_E4F6, sub_DA51 (sound-effect trigger checks -- see dat_C8F8), sub_DEFD, sub_DCFF, sub_EB74, sub_EE3B, sub_F1D6, sub_F476, sub_F00F, sub_E8FF. None of these are individually named by content yet except sub_DA51's role, inferred from what it calls.
comments.rom:C7FC: CONFIRMED (static init loop + LIVE, tools/probe-ram-snapshots.lua, run-01.inp), and now independently re-confirmed byte-for-byte against our own listing (see rom:DDA9's note): builds the centipede. Loop runs X=0 while X<ram_0044 (a generic zero-page temp, not renamed -- reused 20 places for unrelated things), writing ObjectStatus,X (seeded from ram_2107 -- an initial status-bits value, e.g. alive/head/direction flags, NOT a row coordinate) and ObjectDir,X (from a running total in ram_0040, advanced each iteration by a fixed step in ram_0042 -- an LCG-shaped generator; also snapshotting the running pointer into ObjectX,X, the segment's real starting X position). LIVE: ObjectStatus ($00D0-$00DB) and ObjectDir ($00E2-$00ED) are each exactly 12 bytes and both churn on nearly every one of 500 one-second snapshots across the whole recording -- matches the classic 12-segment centipede exactly, though what churns is status/direction bits, not literal position. After the loop, segment 0 (the head) gets its status/dir perturbed specially (EOR on ObjectDir, ORA on ObjectStatus) -- setting its canonical head/alive/direction bits rather than the loop's generic placement. RETRACTION: ObjectStatus/ObjectDir were previously named CentipedeSegRow/CentipedeSegCol on the theory the churn was position data. It's not -- ObjectStatus is a per-object status-bits byte (bit7 alive, bit6 poisoned, bit5 head, bits1-0 turn-stage, etc.) and ObjectDir encodes direction/graphics-offset (bit2 = facing left), for an 18-slot general object table shared by the centipede, spider, flea/scorpion, the player's shooter, and its shot -- not centipede-specific, and not raw coordinates. The real per-object pixel position is ObjectX/ObjectY ($005C/$006E), barely touched in this project before now. Independently verified: rom:F30A's exact byte sequence (`AND #$FC / CMP #$4C / BNE... / ORA #$E7` acting on ObjectStatus, preceded by reads of ObjectX and ObjectY) is the poison-mushroom collision check -- ObjectStatus bit 6 is the poisoned flag, and being poisoned forces the segment into a continuous-turning state (matching the classic 'poisoned segments rush straight down' behavior), not merely a hint any more.
comments.rom:F30A: CONFIRMED, independently re-derived (see rom:C7FC's note): the poison-mushroom collision check. `AND #$FC / CMP #$4C` tests the specific character/tile value just collided with (from a preceding COBSTAC-equivalent lookup, not yet itself named/labeled in this listing); on a match, `ObjectStatus,X / ORA #$E7 / STA ObjectStatus,X` sets the head's poisoned bit (bit 6) along with its alive/head/turn-stage bits. This is what actually drives the erratic-movement behavior the user described -- a poisoned head is forced into continuous turning elsewhere in this routine, not handled by a separate 'erratic movement' mechanism as originally guessed.
comments.rom:C825: Segment-count-mismatch branch, right after the build loop above: if the number of segments just placed (the loop's final count) doesn't equal CentipedeSegTarget (rom:sub_D8D5's dat_D97D-seeded value), falls through to more setup instead of the rom:C8A0 skip. Related to, but not the same mechanism as, the bottom-of-screen multi-head-spawn the user described -- see rom:NewHeadFlag's note for the actual spawn logic (ram_2112/2114/2115), found via the reference cross-check and independently spotted at rom:C7BE/rom:D907/rom:DDE2 in our own listing.
comments.rom:C7BE: NewHeadCount/NewHeadTimer/NewHeadFlag ($2112/$2114/$2115) -- the bottom-of-screen looping/multi-head-spawn mechanic the user specifically described watching ("centipede heads spawn" when it loops at the bottom). Found via cross-checking a private, unofficial preserved-source archive of GCC's original assembly (not quoted/redistributed -- see docs/FINDINGS.md), then independently spotted at the exact same addresses in our own listing: here (`LDA ram_2112,Y / STA ram_2114 / ... / STA ram_2115`, matching a seed-the-timer-and-clear-the-flag pattern), and at rom:DDE2/rom:D907 (adjusting the count, capped/reset via SBC #$02 with a $30/$C0 floor-and-reset, matching a difficulty-dependent 'heads come out faster over time' ramp). Mechanism, reconstructed from the shape our own code follows: a segment reaching the bottom row while it's a head sets NewHeadFlag; a separate routine (not yet located byte-for-byte in our listing) counts NewHeadTimer down, and at zero, finds a free slot in the object table and spawns a brand-new centipede head there, incrementing SegmentsRemaining and shrinking NewHeadCount so subsequent spawns arrive faster. Not yet independently traced end-to-end the way rom:C7FC was -- the seed/reset points are confirmed, the actual spawn routine itself is not yet located in our own code.
comments.rom:DCFF: ram_2129 (FLAGS). Bit 6 confirmed (see docs/FINDINGS.md) as a mushroom-restoration-in-progress flag -- during certain wave transitions, empty mushroom-field cells get refilled. Matches this session's earlier live observation of six brief (~1 second) pulses across run-01.inp, previously catalogued only as 'a notable event, unclear which.' Bit 7 (unconfirmed in our own code) is reportedly 'a player's game has ended, in 2-player mode' per the reference cross-check -- not independently checked, since run-01.inp never exercised 2-player mode.
comments.rom:C79B: ram_2122. RETRACTION: previously guessed as a 'current player turn index' on the strength of staying flat at 0 for this 1-player recording. Cross-checking a private reference archive suggests it's actually a game-type/mode selector (1-player vs. 2-player variants, including a 2-player team-play bit) -- which would also explain staying at a fixed value for an entire 1-player session, just not for the reason guessed. Not independently re-derived from our own code this pass; flagged as corrected-by-reference rather than reconfirmed.
comments.rom:E728: CONFIRMED shape, not yet named: looks like new-life/new-wave setup -- clears ram_00DC/ram_00DD and ram_1FC7 bit 7, then seeds several position-pair variables (ram_006A-6D, ram_007C-7F, ram_00F0/F1) with fixed constants. Candidate for player-ship and/or flea/scorpion starting positions; not confirmed against live position data this pass.
comments.rom:ED45: VEC_ED45/VEC_ED64. CONFIRMED, now found automatically by the ram_vectors scan alone (no manual `entries` needed -- see the a7800-toolkit fix below): a two-handler DLI ping-pong chain through ram_00F4/ram_00F5, the exact same mechanism Ballblazer used. VEC_ED45 sets CTRL=$40, CHARBASE=$C1 (inside chr_rom_C2AC) then re-arms itself to VEC_ED64 for the next interrupt. VEC_ED64 sets CTRL=$4B, CHARBASE=$39 (a different MARIA graphics-bank value, not yet mapped to a ROM range), increments the frame counter (ram_2100), calls sub_CD16/sub_F1D6/sub_CEE5, then re-arms VEC_ED45. A third writer (rom:D883/rom:E2EE, setting $C298 -- the 'normal' per-frame handler) was already found the same way. TOOLKIT FIX: `disasm.py`'s scan_ram_vectors originally only tracked LDA-imm/STA pairs; VEC_ED45's own store of the $ED64 target uses LDA (lo byte) + LDY (hi byte) into STA + STY, a mixed-register form the scanner didn't follow, so with only that gap fixed on our end (adding rom:ED45/rom:ED64 to `entries` by hand) the *reason* stayed a latent toolkit limitation. Fixed at the root instead: the scanner now tracks A/X/Y independently and matches any ST{A,X,Y} against the corresponding register's last LD{A,X,Y} #imm. Verified against both this project (identical result, no manual entries needed) and Ballblazer (round-trip still passes; coverage went up slightly, 58.5%->58.9%, from a previously-missed mixed-register vector there too).
comments.rom:CD16: sub_CD16/sub_CD68: the per-row MARIA zone slot allocator, and (via sub_CD68) the centipede's own renderer. sub_CD16 resets a 22-entry table of zone base pointers (ram_1825, ram_1874, ... ram_1EEA, each ~79 bytes apart, spanning the $18xx-$1Exx display-list zone pages) and a parallel 23-byte 'slots used per zone' counter array at ram_0044-ram_005A (ram_0044 is reused elsewhere as a plain zero-page temp too -- this is a second, distinct use, not a naming conflict in the ROM, just in this annotation's choice not to rename a heavily-overloaded byte). sub_CD68 reads ObjectStatus,X, maps it to a zone index (row>>3-ish, derived from the object's live position by then, not the status bits directly -- worth re-checking exactly which field feeds this now that ObjectStatus/ObjectX/ObjectY are properly distinguished), checks that zone's slot counter against a capacity limit (#$45), and computes a display-list address for the segment from dat_C0B0,Y/dat_C098,Y (the same per-zone base tables sub_DB6C uses), advancing the zone's slot counter. This is very likely the general-purpose object-to-zone placer, not centipede-specific, given how generic the mechanism is; only the centipede's call into it has been traced so far.

headers.rom:C000: chr_rom_C000/chr_rom_C2AC. CONFIRMED (not guessed): both writers of CHARBASE (rom:D88D, rom:EC75) load #$C0 immediately before the write, so this is the real indirect-mode character set base, not just a visual match. gfx.py's default indirect-mode render at $C000 shows a readable digit/letter set followed by recognizable game sprites. DOUBLE RETRACTION this session, both caught while tracing gameplay logic, both left visible rather than silently fixed: (1) an earlier pass extended this block's end all the way to $CEE5 on the strength of live display-list refs scattered up to $CEE4, reasoning 'one continuous sheet, no gap' -- wrong, it never checked whether anything inside was also a JSR/JMP *target*. rom:C798, rom:C8AC, rom:C8D5 and rom:C8F8 (a heavily-used sound-effect dispatcher, called from 13 places in the real game loop, e.g. sub_DA51) are all real code. (2) the immediate fix (shrinking the block to end at rom:C798) was ITSELF still wrong in a worse way: it left a `gfx:true` declaration spanning ENTRY_Irq (rom:C2AB) -- and disasm.py's forced_data check unconditionally wins over an `entries` seed (see tools/disasm.py's trace loop: `if loc in self.forced_data: break`, checked before the opcode is even read), so the declared block had been silently suppressing the IRQ handler's own disassembly the whole time, label and all -- it showed as `.byte $40` under an `ENTRY_Irq:` label instead of `RTI`. Caught by noticing the entry point rendered as data at all, which should never happen for a hardware-vector-confirmed entry. Fixed by removing the block outright and re-deriving boundaries only from what the unblocked tracer and the live evidence actually agree on: ENTRY_Irq is genuinely one byte (`RTI` -- this cartridge doesn't use POKEY's IRQ features, matching the ROM notes), sitting as an isolated one-byte code island in the middle of the character sheet. The sheet itself is now two blocks either side of it -- chr_rom_C000 ($C000-$C2AA) and chr_rom_C2AC ($C2AC-$C797, tile data through $C796, zero-padded tail, code starts cleanly at $C798) -- both with dense live display-list refs on both sides of the IRQ byte, confirming the split rather than assuming it. Lesson for this ROM specifically: a `gfx:true` block is a hard override, not a hint -- never let one span a confirmed entry point, and after declaring one, grep every `dat_<addr>` label it creates against `J(SR|MP)` in the regenerated listing before trusting the boundary. The '©1984 ATARI' copyright text and enemy sprite fragments render inside the two chr_rom blocks as an indirect-mode grid. CORRECTED 2026-11-08 (a third correction, code-read from the ROM bytes and the regenerated listing, not live): the two-block split above was still wrong. Each of the eight line pages $C000-$C7FF holds tile data only in bytes $00-$97; bytes $98-$FF of every page are code or tables, and nothing but MARIA reads $00-$97 (no label, table base or JSR/JMP target lands there). The tails hold: zone address tables at $C098 (dat_C098), the DLL template at $C198 (dat_C198), the three-stage DLI chain at $C298-$C2F2 (VEC_C298/VEC_C2AC/VEC_C2DA -- ENTRY_Irq at $C2AB is stage 1's closing RTI, not a lone byte, see rom:C2AB), the score-digit writer sub_C398, the palette loader sub_C498, message text at $C598 and $C698, and the start of sub_C798. The two old blocks hid all of it, and today's disasm.py says so when run on them ('2 traces ran into a declared data block and stopped there (first: rom:C298, rom:C498)'). Now eight 152-byte gfx blocks (chr_rom_C000 ... chr_rom_C700) plus data blocks for the tables; the DLI chain and the routines are reached by the ram_vectors scan and their JSRs, with no manual entries. Coverage 50.9% -> 53.8%. The last few bytes of some tails ($C0FE-$C0FF, $C1F7-$C1FF, $C2F3-$C2FF, $C3FD-$C3FF, $C4DC-$C4FF, $C5F5-$C5FF, $C6FC-$C6FF) have no reader found and stay gaps. The 'dense live display-list refs on both sides of the IRQ byte' above were header addresses, which show where objects start, not that every byte between them is graphics.
headers.rom:C098: dat_C098: page-tail tables (code-read 2026-11-08; inside chr_rom_C000 until then). $C098/$C0B0: hi/lo bytes of the 24 zone display lists ($180E, $181F, $186E ... $1EE9, the same lists dat_C198 points at), read by sub_CD68 and sub_DB6C; $C09D/$C0B5 are the same two tables from entry 5 on (rom:CE87, rom:DBA4). $C0C8/$C0DF: hi/lo bytes of 23 rows of the character map at $24AA, $1F bytes per row (rom:DA3D, rom:DB7A, rom:DCC2). $C0F6: the bit masks $01-$80 (rom:C857).
headers.rom:C198: dat_C198: the DLL template (code-read 2026-11-08; inside chr_rom_C000 until then). rom:D88F-D8A0 copies its first 95 bytes to $1F38 and points DPPH/DPPL there. Three-byte entries: a 16-line and two 8-line zones, a 1-line zone, 23 8-line zones whose lists are dat_C098's ($181F ... $1EE9, entry byte $27 = H8 holey DMA, 8 lines; the first is $A7, flagged for a DLI), a 1-line zone, then a 15-line zone flagged for a DLI ($AE), an 8-line zone and a 1-line zone flagged for a DLI ($A0). Three DLI flags, matching the three stages at $C298. The copy stops two bytes into one more entry ($00 $D0); its third byte in RAM is $1F97, which sub_C8F8 uses -- whether MARIA ever reaches that entry was not checked.
headers.rom:C298: The DLI chain (code-read 2026-11-08; inside chr_rom_C000 until then, rendered as data under the VEC_C298 label). ENTRY_Nmi does PHA / JMP ($00F4). Stage 1, VEC_C298 (armed at boot by rom:D883, also by rom:E2EE, and re-armed by stage 3): arms VEC_C2AC, WSYNC, CTRL=$40, writes $80 to $01, PLA / RTI. Stage 2, VEC_C2AC: saves X and Y, arms VEC_C2DA, writes $00 to $01, two WSYNCs, CTRL=$43, then does the per-frame work: sub_CEE5, sub_C398 (score digits), sub_CD10 (the zone rebuild, run only when the main loop has set ram_2108 bit 7 at rom:D868; cleared at rom:CEB2), sub_C498 (palette loader), sub_C946 (sound tick). Stage 3, VEC_C2DA: waits for vblank (sub_D87A), BACKGRND=0, re-arms VEC_C298 and leaves through stage 2's exit at L_C2D4. VEC_ED45/VEC_ED64 (rom:ED45) are a separate two-stage chain through the same vector.
headers.rom:C398: sub_C398 (code-read 2026-11-08; inside chr_rom_C2AC until then): writes 6-digit scores into the character map at $24AA as character indices, leading zeros blanked with $40. Each call of sub_C3C1 reads three BCD bytes 7 apart, high byte first: X=$0E reads $008E, $0087, $0080; X=$0F (when ram_2122 is non-zero) and X=$10 (when ram_2122=3) the next two; otherwise X=$11+ram_1FCB. That is the byte order of rom:DDA9's ADC chain (Score0,X low, Score1,X middle, Score2Team,X high), which does not fit rom:DDA9's retraction note ('each of the four is its own 3-byte number'); that note was not re-checked in this pass.
headers.rom:C498: sub_C498, the palette loader (code-read 2026-11-08; inside chr_rom_C2AC until then), called from DLI stage 2 and from rom:EDA1. One-shot timer: it does nothing while ram_2121 is negative; otherwise it counts it down and, when it passes zero, waits for vblank (sub_D87A) and copies 12 bytes from $F4F2 + ram_211F,X (X = CurrentPlayer, or 0 when ram_2122 >= 2) into P6C1-P6C3, P5, P4 and P3, stopping early once X drops below ram_1FD1. The $F4F2 rows sit at the start of the $F4F2-$FFFF gap that the rom:F4F2 note calls a graphics region -- a lead for that note, not checked here.
headers.rom:C598: dat_C598/dat_C59C (code-read 2026-11-08; inside chr_rom_C2AC until then): lo/hi pointers, indexed by ram_2122, to 23-byte message lines in character indices ($40 = blank) at $C5A0-$C5F4, some overlapping; rom:D9B8 copies the chosen line to $2680.
headers.rom:C698: dat_C698 and the tables after it (code-read 2026-11-08; inside chr_rom_C2AC until then), all text in character indices except the last two: $C698, 15 bytes copied to $26A3 when ram_1FD3 is set (rom:D9D3); $C6A7/$C6AB, lo/hi pointers by ram_1FCB to short lines at $C6AF-$C6CA, with destination offsets at $C6CB and lengths-1 at $C6CF, copied to $26D8 (rom:D99A); $C6D3 (13 bytes, also 9 at rom:E7CF) and $C6E9 (13 bytes) copied to $2665, $C6E0 (9 bytes) to $2629; $C6F6 and $C6F9, two 3-entry tables (rom:EA32, rom:EA62).
headers.rom:D000: GameSpritesB. CONFIRMED LIVE (tools/live-slots.lua, run-01.inp, same session as chr_rom_C000): a second, separate direct-mode sprite sheet, referenced from all 8 line-planar pages ($D000, $D100, ... $D700 -- the classic base+n*256 pattern for an 8-line-tall object) with real widths seen at every page, not a guess from byte patterns alone. Sits between chr_rom_C2AC and ENTRY_Nmi (already-confirmed real code at $D800) with no gap either side. Checked for the same JSR/JMP-into-the-block bug found in chr_rom_C000: none found (grep for `J(SR|MP)\s+dat_D[0-7]` across the whole listing is empty), so this block's boundary is not suspect the same way. Not yet identified by content (which enemy or effect these specific graphics belong to) -- that needs a screenshot cross-check against a chosen frame's live display list, not attempted this pass.
headers.rom:C946: The $C946-$CEE4 gap, right after chr_rom_C2AC's code interruption and right before sub_CEE5 (real code, reached via rom:E2FC). Checked the same way as the F4F2 gap below: no JSR/JMP in the whole listing targets anything inside this range, but the live display-list walk (tools/live-slots.lua, run-01.inp) found two genuine runtime-constructed graphics references landing in it -- $C9A8 (width 21) and $CEC6 (width 31, running exactly to $CEE5 with zero padding, i.e. touching sub_CEE5 with no gap at all). Declared only those two confirmed spans as gfx blocks (gfx_C9A8, gfx_CEC6); the rest of the 1439 bytes stays an honest, unconfirmed gap on the same reasoning as $F4F2-$FFFF -- sparse live evidence inside a range is enough to call its *character* (graphics, not missed code) but not enough to claim the whole span without guessing. CORRECTED 2026-11-08 (code-read from the ROM bytes and the regenerated listing): $C946-$C9A7 is not a gap and gfx_C9A8 was not graphics. $C946 is sub_C946, the per-frame sound tick, called from DLI stage 2 at rom:C2D1 and running to the RTS at $CA26. It steps both TIA voices (X=1,0) through the current effect's streams: effect id in $2775,X (bit 7 = start pending, $FF = idle, set by the sub_C8F8 dispatcher), frequency-stream pointers at $F582/$F58A, AUDV streams at $F592/$F59A, AUDC streams at $F5A2/$F5AA, default durations at $F5B2. Frequency-stream codes: $FF ends the effect and silences the voice, $FE restarts it, $FD nn chains to effect nn, a byte with bit 7 set is followed by an explicit duration and then the note; in the AUDV/AUDC streams a byte with bit 7 set holds its value. When effect 5 starts again it resumes from the stream position saved in $277D (rom:C975; saved when the voice was stolen at rom:C92E). The 'confirmed live' gfx_C9A8 block ($C9A8-$C9BC) began on this routine's CMP #$FF and has been removed. Why the live walk named $C9A8: tools/live-slots.lua records each display-list header's address field, not bytes MARIA was seen to fetch, and this game's headers need not point at the bytes they draw (the object placer writes $C0+fine for the upper zone and 8 pages lower for the zone below, rom:CDF5-CDF9), so a header address alone does not show that the bytes at that address are graphics. Which builder wrote the $C9A8 header was not traced. The same caveat applies to the other live-only blocks (gfx_CEC6, gfx_FE0C, gfx_FE64, gfx_FF24); they were not re-checked in this pass. Lead, not declared here: the sound tables ($F582-$F5C1, with priorities at $F5BA read by sub_C8F8) and the palette loader's colour rows ($F4F2, see rom:C498) sit inside the $F4F2-$FFFF 'graphics region' below. $CA27-$CD0F stays an open gap.
headers.rom:F4F2: The $F4F2-$FFFF gap. Investigated two ways this session: (1) a PC-tagged read-tap on the whole range (tools/probe-gap-readers.lua, run-01.inp, 1,183,549 hits) -- every representative top-hit PC checked resolved to either a busy-wait loop (rom:D861 BIT ram_2108/BMI L_D861) or an address that falls inside the already-confirmed chr_rom_C000 block (impossible as a real 6502 PC) -- i.e. MARIA DMA misattribution artifacts, not real readers (see docs/pitfalls.md in the toolkit). Trial entries at rom:F900 and rom:F902 both failed to produce a sustained instruction trace. (2) tools/live-slots.lua's own display-list walk -- the same live method that confirmed chr_rom_C000 and GameSpritesB -- found three genuine runtime-constructed graphics-object references landing inside this range: $FE0C (width 31), $FE64 (width 30), $FF24 (width 17); see the gfx_FE0C/gfx_FE64/gfx_FF24 blocks. Conclusion: this is a graphics region, not unreached code -- but run-01.inp only exercised a small fraction of it (3 confirmed starts out of 2830 bytes), so most of the range stays an honest, unconfirmed gap rather than a guessed block. A recording that reaches more enemy/bonus varieties, or 2-player mode, would likely close more of it.
